named.name: Hazor
named.label: right
named.note: Tel Hazor, the largest city of Canaan at the time, "head of all those kingdoms" (11:10). Excavations found a great destruction by fire in the 13th century BC.

named.name: Madon
named.label: right
named.note: Site uncertain; OpenBible links it with Merom.

named.name: Merom
named.label: left
named.note: Where the kings camped (11:5). The site is debated: suggestions include springs near Meron in Upper Galilee and sites farther north.

moves.text: Jabin of Hazor and the northern kings gather at the Waters of Merom
Joshua comes suddenly and falls on them
Pursuit to Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim
Pursuit east to the Valley of Mizpeh
Joshua turns back and takes Hazor

symbols.key: Battle at the Waters of Merom
Hazor burned; the other cities left standing

p: Israel burned none of the cities "that stood on their mounds" except Hazor (11:13). At Tel Hazor the great Late Bronze city ended in a fierce fire; scholars debate whether to link that destruction with Joshua, with later conflicts, or with internal revolt.

About the routes. Places are located from OpenBible.info. The lines between them are reconstructions drawn for teaching, not paths the text describes. Where the kings came from is shown only for the cities whose sites are reasonably known.
